note: [L] proves the product rule only for three finite ℕ-supported weights, in expanded form, with e(+nα) instead of e(-αn); there is no statement of the two-factor rule as such.

snippet.text:
have key : ∀ α : ℝ, expSum X a α * expSum X b α * expSum X c α * e (-(N * α)) =
      ∑ n₁ ∈ range (X + 1), ∑ n₂ ∈ range (X + 1), ∑ n₃ ∈ range (X + 1),
        a n₁ * b n₂ * c n₃ * e (((n₁ + n₂ + n₃ : ℕ) - N : ℤ) * α) := by
    intro α
    rw [expSum, expSum, expSum, sum_mul_sum, sum_mul, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun n₁ _ => ?_
    rw [sum_mul, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun n₂ _ => ?_
    rw [mul_sum, sum_mul]
    refine sum_congr rfl fun n₃ _ => ?_
    have : (((n₁ + n₂ + n₃ : ℕ) - N : ℤ) : ℝ) * α = n₁ * α + n₂ * α + n₃ * α + -(N * α) := by
      push_cast; ring
    rw [this, e_add, e_add, e_add]
    ring

proof_context.conclusion: The product `S_a S_b S_c e(-Nα)` of exponential sums expands to `∑ a(n₁)b(n₂)c(n₃) e((n₁+n₂+n₃-N)α)`, the coefficient-level form of transform of a convolution equals the product of transforms (three factors).
